title: Wire RecipeCatalog into AppRoot lifecycle
description: Instantiate `RecipeCatalog` at the app root, inject it into the SwiftUI environment, and trigger catalog loads from the folder-selection lifecycle alongside the existing store and aisle catalog wiring.
acceptance_criteria: `AppRoot` owns a single `RecipeCatalog` instance for the app session.
`RecipeCatalog` is injected with `.environment(...)` so descendant recipe views can read it from the environment.
Folder URL changes trigger catalog loading/reloading from the app root lifecycle.

handoff_summary.completed: All three acceptance criteria met: AppRoot owns a single RecipeCatalog instance, it is injected into the SwiftUI environment, and folder URL changes trigger catalog loading.
handoff_summary.risks: SourceKit diagnostics in the worktree flagged all pre-existing types (RecipesFolderStore, AisleCatalog, FolderSetupView, etc.) as unfound — confirmed to be a worktree LSP index issue, not real compilation errors. The changes are structurally identical to the existing AisleCatalog wiring.
handoff_summary.next_action: Tester agent can now verify RecipeCatalog is accessible from descendant recipe views via the environment.
handoff_summary.conflict_risks: None — changes are confined to AppRoot.swift and are additive only.
handoff_summary.design_decisions: Reused the existing single `.task(id: store.folderURL)` closure rather than adding a separate one, keeping the folder-URL reaction logic in one place.
handoff_summary.test_coverage_notes: No tests run per developer guardrails. Tester agent should verify: RecipeCatalog is readable from @Environment in a recipe view, and that load() is called on folder URL change.
handoff_summary.known_limitations: RecipeCatalog has no EnvironmentKey — it relies on SwiftUI's Observable-based environment injection (@Observable + .environment()). This is correct for Swift 5.9+ / iOS 17+.

conflict_risks: None — changes are confined to AppRoot.swift and are additive only.

execution_history.summary: Wired `RecipeCatalog` into `AppRoot` following the existing `AisleCatalog` pattern: added `@State private var recipeCatalog = RecipeCatalog()`, injected it via `.environment(recipeCatalog)`, and added `recipeCatalog.load(from: url)` inside the existing `.task(id: store.folderURL)` closure so catalog reloads whenever the folder URL changes.
